newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger on jobs data, dlr gain.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger on jobs data, dlr gain.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much stronger on Thursday, outperforming U.S. treasuries in parts of the curve, with a tame U.S. jobs report and a rally in the Canadian dollar helping boost prices, analysts said.

"It was combination of factors. One was a market-friendly U.S. payroll employment report today on the heels of yesterday's decision by the FOMC not to raise rates," said Michael Gregory, fixed-income economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.25 to C$116.80 to yield 6.692 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 1-3/32 to yield 6.62 percent. The spread between the bonds was seven basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Wednesday.

North American fixed-income markets strengthened this morning after the U.S. Labor Department said payrolls rose by 217,000 in June, while the unemployment rate ticked up to 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent. A survey of economists had forecast a rise of 222,000 and a steady jobless rate.
The Canadian market also benefited from gains in the Canadian dollar after the report, which helped reduce expectations of a near-term U.S. rate increase.
"With the Canadian dollar still basking in the glow of last week's rate hike, it caused us to even outperform the U.S. today," said Lehman's Gregory.

While trading was active earlier in the session, activity died down toward the end of the day with the U.S. market closing early ahead of the July 4 Independence Day holiday. Activity in Canada was expected to be light on Friday amid the absence of a U.S. market.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.73 to C$108.32 to yield 6.114 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which rose 24/32 to yield 6.30 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 19 basis points from 20 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.07 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.15 percent.
